text:
Ottawa has points in eight straight (6-0-2), and this run is not a goalie carrying a mediocre team. The Senators took 59% of the expected goals over those games (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and they are at 54% at five on five for the season. Linus Ullmark is still the headline: .937 and 10.6 goals saved above expected in 12 games, a year after he finished 13.3 below expected. Our numbers give Ottawa a 91% playoff chance.

Tim Stützle has made William Eklund's injury (ankle, out until about January) look manageable. He moved onto the line with Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund and has eight points (four goals) in a five-game point streak. Cozens and Zetterlund are both among our Sleepers tonight. The front office may not be done: Elliotte Friedman linked the Senators to Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, as Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe relayed, and Drake Batherson went the other way with his recruiting, per Daily Faceoff: "Sidney Crosby 'can have my house' if he comes to Senators."

Calgary opens a five-game road trip in a hole. The Flames have a -24 goal difference on -12.7 expected, take 46% of the five-on-five expected goals, and our numbers have them at 9% to make the playoffs. Dustin Wolf (.877, 6.5 goals below expected) has not bailed them out, and Kevin Bahl's season-ending injury thinned the blue line. Saturday's 4-3 overtime loss to Chicago, won by Sam Rinzel, fit the pattern. Matt Coronato has two points in his last ten when his ice time says about 7.6. One brighter note is rookie Jonathan Castagna, who scored his first two NHL goals in San Jose last week. Connor Zary is off ESPN's injury report.

We have Ottawa at 3.81 expected goals and Calgary at 2.34. For the Flames, a tight game into the third would already count as progress.
headline: Senators' hot run meets a Flames team in trouble
